records.name: Fleisher Art Memorial
records.summary: An art center in Bella Vista where adults take fall and winter art classes and kids and teens join youth programs. It also holds open community events such as a Day of the Dead celebration and a cultural market.
records.what_you_do: Sign up for a term class or workshop, bring a child to a youth program, or come to a community festival.

schedule.text: Adult classes run in a fall term (Fall 2026) and a winter term (Winter 2027). A Young Artist Program runs in fall 2026 for kids, and a Teen Lounge runs 2026 to 2027.

cost.text: Class fees are not listed on the site. Tuition assistance is offered, and donations and memberships are accepted.

first_step.how: Browse the class listings and register through the registration site linked from fleisher.org
first_step.basis: Classes are open to the public with an online sign up, but skill levels and fees are not spelled out on the site.

records.notes: The site does not list a phone number or email. Painting and drawing come from a list article's description of the center, not the center's own program list. Its tax status is not stated, so kind is set to program.

records.name: The Arts League
records.summary: A contemporary art center in West Philadelphia, also listed as the University City Arts League. Artists teach adult classes and workshops, members can use open studio time, and kids can join an after school art program.
records.what_you_do: Take an artist led class or workshop, use the open studio, or sign a child up for after school art.

schedule.text: Adult classes run through the year. An exhibition called BOHÉMIENNE runs October 2 to 29, 2026, and the event post was dated September 11, 2026.

cost.text: Class prices, membership prices and scholarship details are not listed on the site.

first_step.how: Use the Take a Class link for adult classes, or the Register link for after school art
first_step.basis: Adult classes are open to the public with online sign up, though the class types are not named on the site.

records.notes: The site gives no street address or phone number, so no location is recorded. The University City Arts League name on list sites points to this organization, but the domain ucal.org did not resolve, so the match is by name only.

records.name: Allens Lane Art Center
records.summary: An art center in Mount Airy with classes for kids ages 5 to 12, for teens, and for adults. It also runs summer camps, a pottery program, and gallery shows with artist talks.
records.what_you_do: Sign up for a semester class, send a child to camp, or come to an opening or artist talk.

schedule.text: Fall 2026 classes began September 8, and registration is open now. A Kids Day Off Camp runs October 9, and gallery events run through October, including an artists' talk on October 24 from 6 to 8 pm.

cost.text: Tuition and scholarship details are not listed on the site.

first_step.how: Find a class in the Fall 2026 listings and register online, or email info@allenslane.org
first_step.basis: Public classes are listed with online sign up for ages 5 and up and for adults.

records.notes: The center's own site does not mention ceramics, so the pottery tag comes from a list article. Office hours are Monday to Thursday, 10 am to 5 pm.

records.name: The Clay Studio
records.summary: A ceramics studio in Kensington with year round classes for beginners through advanced makers, kids summer camps, and free hands on clay sessions for the public. Tuition help is available.
records.what_you_do: Take a handbuilding or wheel class, join a workshop or summer camp, or come to a free clay session or a Thursday talk.

schedule.text: Classes run year round. Gallery and shop hours are weekdays 11 am to 5:30 pm and weekends 11 am to 5 pm. There is an evening open house on the second Thursday of each month from 5 to 8 pm, and Clay and Conversations talks run on Thursdays.

cost.text: Class prices are not listed. Tuition assistance is available for classes, workshops and summer camps.

first_step.how: Email info@theclaystudio.org or call 215-925-3453 to sign up for a class
first_step.basis: Beginner classes and free public clay sessions are listed, with tuition assistance available.

records.notes: The site lists recurring events with no dates, so status is probably_active. It does not state its tax status, so kind is set to program. Pottery is the only interest tag because the site lists no painting or drawing classes.

records.name: The Halide Project
records.summary: A community darkroom in Kensington where people learn black and white and film photography. Newcomers take an orientation class first, and the darkroom has a pay what you can model.
records.what_you_do: Take the new member orientation, then book darkroom time to develop film and make prints. Members also show work in a yearly member exhibition.

schedule.text: Opening hours are not listed. New members take an orientation before using the darkroom. A Darkroom Member Exhibition is planned for 2026.

cost.text: Pay what you can, according to a 2022 news article. Current rates are not shown on the site.

first_step.how: Sign up for the New Member Orientation through the site, then book darkroom time
first_step.basis: A newcomer orientation comes before darkroom use, and the group says how to start.

records.notes: The site's events have no dates. Pricing and the orientation detail come from an October 2022 article, so confirm current rates. Membership terms are not stated on the site.

records.name: Mission in Arts Clay Studio
records.summary: A member supported clay studio in Kensington. Members pay a monthly fee for wheel and studio time, kiln firings, and their own shelf space, with open studio hours Thursday to Sunday evenings.
records.what_you_do: Apply for membership, meet the studio on a visit, then make work during open studio hours and join the occasional handbuilding workshop.

schedule.text: Open studio Thursday to Sunday, 4 to 7 pm. Members also get 24 hour key access.

cost.text: $120 per month with a three month commitment, billed monthly. New members get 25 pounds of clay and kiln firing is included.

first_step.how: Fill out the online membership form, then schedule a studio visit
first_step.basis: You need to apply, visit, and pay monthly dues before you can use the studio, and the form asks about your clay experience.

records.notes: No phone or email is listed outside the online form. The workshop section names no current offerings. Fees are for a membership, so the cost is shown as paid.

records.name: Outlaw Arts
records.summary: A shared clay studio in Mount Airy with six week beginner courses in handbuilding and wheel throwing. Membership is for experienced clay users, and reduced fees are offered to some local residents.
records.what_you_do: Take a beginner course, then move into the shared studio once you have enough experience and finish the introduction period.

schedule.text: Six week beginner courses run in handbuilding and wheel throwing. Membership is for intermediate and advanced clay users.

cost.text: Class and membership prices are not listed. Reduced fees are offered to some local residents.

first_step.how: Contact the studio manager at cornelia@outlaw-arts.com or (267) 650-1757 to register or join the waiting list
first_step.basis: Beginner courses are open to the public, and the page gives a direct contact to sign up.

records.notes: Event listings on the site have no year. The site mentions teen classes without details, and the list article says it takes kids ages 4 to 12. Membership needs about ten weeks of recent clay experience.

records.name: Scribe Video Center
records.summary: A nonprofit media arts center in West Philadelphia that helps people make community films. It runs adult workshops, such as a speculative fiction scriptwriting course, and hosts screenings and learning sessions.
records.what_you_do: Take a workshop, come to a screening, or join as a member to support the center's community programs.

schedule.text: New Moons, New Suns scriptwriting course: five Tuesdays, 7 to 9 pm, October 27, November 3, 10, 17 and 24, 2026. A screening of a work in progress is on Friday, October 23 at 7 pm, and a learning session on direct cinema is on Friday, October 30 from 5 to 7 pm.

cost.text: Workshop fees and scholarships are not listed on the site. Membership is offered, with prices not shown.

first_step.how: Register for a workshop or screening through the links on scribe.org
first_step.basis: Public workshops and screenings have online registration, though the site does not say what skill level they need.

records.notes: Older listings show other addresses, including 4212 Chestnut Street. This record uses the address on the center's own page. The Film Scholars Program is named on the site but no details are given.

records.name: VC Philadelphia
records.summary: The Philadelphia chapter of the Video Consortium, a network for nonfiction filmmakers. It holds in person gatherings each month with screenings, panels, workshops and happy hours.
records.what_you_do: Come to a monthly gathering to meet other filmmakers and hear about jobs and resources.

schedule.text: Monthly in person gatherings. The next is a Fireside screening of DERAILED on Wednesday, October 14, 2026 at 6 pm at The Philadelphia Inquirer, 100 South Independence Mall West.

cost.text: The page does not say whether joining or attending costs money.

first_step.how: Click Join VC or sign up for an upcoming gathering from the events page
first_step.basis: Gatherings are posted publicly with a join link, though membership terms are not stated.

records.notes: The hub page is short, so the nonfiction focus rests on the chapter's description in a search result. Its audience is working filmmakers, so the crowd tag is professionals.

records.name: Photographic Society of Philadelphia
records.summary: A photography club founded in 1862 that shows member work in online galleries and holds a yearly salon. Joining is by paid membership.
records.what_you_do: Join or renew your membership, post your photographs in the member galleries, and go to club events.

schedule.text: Member galleries show 2025 and 2026 images and a 2025 salon. The meeting and events pages are linked but did not show dates in the fetched text.

cost.text: Membership requires paid dues, and the amounts are not shown on the pages fetched.

first_step.how: Use the join or renew link on the site to apply for membership
first_step.basis: Joining needs dues and an application, and the meeting schedule was not visible before you join.

records.notes: The page tagline gives the 1862 founding. No phone, email or meeting place was visible in the fetched text. A search result listed a third Tuesday meeting at a club building, but the site did not confirm it, so it is not recorded.

records.name: Philadelphia Guild of Handweavers
records.summary: A fiber arts guild in Manayunk, founded in 1952, where members weave, spin, felt, dye, knit, crochet and sew. Members meet monthly and join small interest groups to help each other build skills.
records.what_you_do: Join the guild, come to the monthly meeting at the Guild House, and take part in an interest group.

schedule.text: Monthly meeting, usually the second Thursday at 7 pm at the Guild House. Special interest groups meet on their own schedules.

cost.text: Membership cost is not stated on the page.

first_step.how: Use the Join link on pghw.org, or call (215) 487-9690 or use the contact form
first_step.basis: The guild has a public join path and open monthly meetings, and it names interest groups for skill building.

records.notes: The page lists no dated events, and the calendar at pghw.org/events did not load into the fetch. Contact emails on the page are hidden, so the contact form is listed instead.

records.name: Philadelphia Community Access Media (PhillyCAM)
records.summary: A community media center on Ranstead Street where residents learn to make television and radio programs. Its free workshops include Create Space, a monthly open session for ages 13 to 18.
records.what_you_do: Take a free workshop, join a youth media session, or become a member to make and air your own program.

schedule.text: A virtual radio orientation runs October 8, 2026 at 6 pm. Create Space: Acting for the Camera runs October 10, 2026 at 1 pm for ages 13 to 18. The center is closed October 12. Monthly Create Space sessions run through the year.

cost.text: Workshops and Create Space sessions are free. Membership cost is not listed.

first_step.how: Call 267.639.5481 or use the Contact Us page, then sign up for a free workshop or member orientation
first_step.basis: Workshops and youth sessions are free and listed publicly, and member orientations are offered for new TV and radio users.

records.notes: The site lists Create Space for ages 13 to 18, so the minimum age is not set for the whole center. Workshop registration requires logging in to a member site. Membership cost is not listed.

records.name: The Philadelphia Sketch Club
records.summary: An artists' club on South Camac Street that runs weekly figure drawing open studios six days a week. Anyone can come for a small fee, and members pay less. Some sessions use a nude model.
records.what_you_do: Bring your own supplies and draw from a live model at a weekly open studio. Monitors collect the fee after the first twenty minutes.

schedule.text: Figure drawing runs Monday and Wednesday evenings from 6:30 to 9:30 pm, Tuesday and Thursday afternoons from noon to 3 pm, Saturday mornings from 9:30 am to 12:30 pm, and Sunday evenings from 5:30 to 8:30 pm. Sessions run weekly except holidays and bad weather.

cost.text: $15 for non-members, $10 for members, and $9 for full-time students with ID. Fees are collected by monitors after the first twenty minutes.

first_step.how: Come to any session. No sign up is needed, and non-members can attend.
first_step.basis: Drop in with no sign up and no membership needed, though the page does not describe a beginner program.

records.notes: The site footer has a misspelled address, so the info@sketchclub.org address is taken from the page's contact link. Guided and self guided tiers were mentioned in a search summary but not on the site, so they are not recorded. The club's gala is its 166th, and it lists a Fall 2026 class, which puts it in 2026.

records.name: Wild Hand
records.summary: A fiber shop in Mount Airy with classes in knitting, crochet, weaving and spinning. It runs a free weekly Fiber Folk Night on Wednesday evenings from 5 to 7 pm.
records.what_you_do: Come to Fiber Folk Night on a Wednesday, or sign up for a beginner class such as community knit or crochet basics.

schedule.text: Fiber Folk Night every Wednesday from 5 to 7 pm, free. Classes are listed on the site for October and November, with some sessions for kids.

cost.text: Fiber Folk Night is free. Classes cost about $10 for community basics and up to $350 for multi day retreats.

first_step.how: Come to Fiber Folk Night, or sign up for a listed beginner class on the shop site
first_step.basis: Free weekly night and beginner classes are listed, though the page does not say how to sign up for the night.

records.notes: Class dates on the site have no year, so status is probably_active rather than active. This is a for profit shop, included because it runs a free weekly community night.
